stem: A new architecture needs a compute service for a short, event-triggered function, and a networking service that routes incoming HTTP requests to different backend instances based on the request's URL path. Which TWO choices satisfy these two requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: AWS Lambda for the short, event-triggered function
An EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum capacity of one instance kept running to handle the triggering event
A Classic Load Balancer distributing requests round-robin across the backend instances
An Application Load Balancer routing HTTP requests by URL path across the backend instances
An EC2 instance running a script that checks once a minute for the triggering condition

rationale: AWS Lambda runs code on demand in response to an event and bills only for compute time consumed, matching the short, event-triggered function requirement. An Application Load Balancer supports path-based routing across a target group, matching the URL-path routing requirement directly. An Auto Scaling group kept at a minimum of one instance running at all times is a standing server the team pays for and patches continuously, rather than compute that runs only when the event occurs. A Classic Load Balancer can distribute requests round-robin across instances, but it does not evaluate the request's URL path the way the routing requirement calls for. An EC2 instance running a script that checks once a minute is polling on an interval rather than reacting immediately to the event, and it still requires the team to operate and patch that instance.
